$comment: The 'everything an app needs' knowledge base. Drives the planning interview (questions) and the audit (verify items). priority: core = always asked, recommended = asked when keywords match the description/answers, optional = only surfaced in the blueprint as considerations.

categories.title: Purpose & audience

questions.question: Who are the primary users of this app, and what is the single most important thing they should be able to do?
questions.why: Everything else (features, design, stack) is prioritized around this.

questions.question: What does success look like? (e.g. 'my team uses it daily', 'paying customers', 'portfolio piece')
questions.why: Determines how much to invest in scale, polish and monetization.

verify: The main user flow works end to end without errors.

categories.title: Device targets & platforms

questions.question: Where should this run? Options: responsive web app / installable PWA / native mobile (App Store & Play Store) / desktop app (Windows, Mac, Linux) / local self-hosted. You can pick multiple.
questions.why: Selects the scaffold: Next.js PWA (web), Expo (native mobile), Tauri (desktop), Docker Compose (local).

verify: App renders correctly on mobile, tablet and desktop viewport sizes.

categories.title: Identity & authentication

questions.question: Do users need accounts/login? If yes: email+password, magic links, social login (Google/GitHub/Apple), or a mix?
questions.why: Auth choice affects the database, session handling and legal requirements.

questions.question: Are there different user roles (e.g. admin, editor, viewer)? What can each role do?
questions.why: Role-based access control must be designed into the data model, not bolted on.

verify: Passwords are hashed (never stored or logged in plain text).
Sessions/tokens expire and can be revoked.
Protected routes reject unauthenticated and unauthorized users (server-side, not just hidden UI).

categories.title: Data model & storage

questions.question: What are the main things the app stores? (e.g. recipes, invoices, workouts) Roughly what fields does each have, and how do they relate?
questions.why: The data model is the backbone; getting it right early avoids painful migrations.

questions.question: Will users upload files or images? Roughly how large and how many?
questions.why: File storage needs size limits, type validation and a storage backend.

questions.question: Should users be able to export or permanently delete their data?
questions.why: Data portability and deletion are both good practice and legally required in many regions.

verify: All user input is validated server-side.
Database queries are parameterized (no SQL injection).
File uploads validate type and size server-side.

categories.title: Core features

questions.question: List the features the first version MUST have. Then list features that would be nice later. Be ruthless: what is the minimum that is genuinely useful?
questions.why: A small excellent v1 beats a large broken one. The nice-to-haves go into the roadmap.

questions.question: Do users need to search or filter content? How (full-text, tags, categories)?
questions.why: Search strategy affects the database and indexing choices.

questions.question: Does anything need to update live without a refresh (chat, collaboration, live dashboards)?
questions.why: Realtime needs websockets/subscriptions, which shapes the backend.

verify: Every must-have feature from the interview exists and works.

categories.title: Payments & monetization

questions.question: Will the app take payments? One-time purchases, subscriptions, or marketplace-style (paying out to others)?
questions.why: Payment model determines the Stripe integration pattern and legal obligations.

verify: Payment secrets live only in server-side environment variables.
Webhooks verify signatures.
Prices/amounts are computed server-side, never trusted from the client.

categories.title: Notifications & communication

questions.question: Should the app send emails, push notifications or reminders? For what events?
questions.why: Transactional email/push needs a provider and unsubscribe handling.

verify: Emails include unsubscribe/notification-preference options where required.

categories.title: Offline & sync

questions.question: Does the app need to work offline or with a poor connection? What must work offline?
questions.why: Offline-first requires local storage plus conflict resolution and changes the architecture.

verify: If offline was requested: core flows work with network disabled and sync on reconnect.

categories.title: Languages & regions

questions.question: Which languages and regions should be supported at launch? Any right-to-left languages?
questions.why: Retro-fitting i18n is expensive; wiring it from day one is cheap.

verify: Dates, numbers and currencies format via locale-aware APIs, not string concatenation.

categories.title: Accessibility

questions.question: Any specific accessibility requirements (e.g. WCAG AA compliance for a public/government audience)? Default: keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels and adequate contrast are always included.
questions.why: Accessibility is a baseline quality gate in the audit, not an optional extra.

verify: All interactive elements are keyboard-reachable and have accessible names.
Color contrast meets WCAG AA.
Images have alt text; forms have labels.

categories.title: SEO & discoverability

questions.question: Are there public pages that should rank on search engines or look good when shared on social media?
questions.why: Public pages need server rendering, meta tags, Open Graph images and a sitemap.

verify: Public pages have titles, meta descriptions, Open Graph tags and a sitemap.

categories.title: Analytics & telemetry

questions.question: Do you want usage analytics? Privacy-friendly (Plausible/Umami) or full-featured (PostHog/GA4)?
questions.why: Analytics choice affects privacy policy and cookie banners.

verify: Analytics respects Do-Not-Track and is disclosed in the privacy policy.

categories.title: Error tracking & logging

questions.question: Should production errors be reported somewhere (e.g. Sentry), or is console/file logging enough for now?
questions.why: You cannot fix what you cannot see; error tracking pays for itself immediately.

verify: Unhandled errors show a friendly error page, never a stack trace.
Logs never contain passwords, tokens or personal data.

categories.title: Security

questions.question: How sensitive is the data (public, personal, financial, medical)? Any compliance needs (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2)?
questions.why: Data sensitivity sets the security bar for encryption, access control and auditing.

verify: No secrets committed to the repository (scanned).
Dependencies have no known critical vulnerabilities (scanned).
Security headers set (CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.).
Rate limiting on auth and expensive endpoints.
HTTPS enforced in production.

categories.title: Performance & optimization

questions.question: Roughly how many users/records should this handle in year one? (10s, 1000s, millions?)
questions.why: Scale expectations decide caching, pagination and infrastructure choices.

verify: Lighthouse performance score >= 80 on key pages.
Images are optimized and lazy-loaded.
Lists are paginated; no unbounded queries.

categories.title: Legal & compliance

questions.question: Does the app need Terms of Service, a Privacy Policy or cookie consent? (If it stores personal data of EU users: yes.) App Factory can generate tailored templates with generate_legal_docs.
questions.why: Legal pages and consent flows must exist before launch, not after.

questions.question: Where are your users located (EU, US/California, India, worldwide)? Could any users be children under 13?
questions.why: Regions determine which regulations apply: GDPR (EU), CCPA/CPRA (California), DPDP (India), COPPA (children under 13).

verify: Privacy policy and terms pages exist and are linked if personal data is stored.
Cookie/tracking consent is collected before non-essential cookies fire (if EU users).
Users can request export and deletion of their data (if GDPR/CCPA applies).

categories.title: Admin & operations

questions.question: Do you (the owner) need an admin area to manage users/content, or is direct database access fine at first?
questions.why: Admin tooling is often forgotten and then urgently needed on launch day.

verify: Admin routes are protected by role checks on the server.

categories.title: Backups & data safety

questions.question: If the database was lost, how much data could you afford to lose — an hour, a day, nothing?
questions.why: Backup frequency and strategy follow directly from this answer.

verify: Automated backups are configured (or documented as a deliberate non-goal).

categories.title: Integrations

questions.question: Should the app connect to any external services (calendars, Slack, existing APIs, spreadsheets)?
questions.why: Integrations often dominate the effort; they must be planned, not improvised.

verify: External API keys are stored server-side and calls have timeouts and error handling.

categories.title: Deployment & hosting

questions.question: How should this be deployed? Options: web hosting (Vercel/Netlify — easiest), your own server via Docker, purely local on your machine, or app stores (mobile). Also: any custom domain?
questions.why: The deploy target shapes environment config, secrets handling and the CI pipeline.

questions.question: What is the monthly hosting budget? (Free tier only, ~$20, or whatever it takes?)
questions.why: Budget decides between free tiers, serverless and dedicated infrastructure.

verify: Environment variables documented in .env.example (no real values).
Production build completes without errors.
Health check endpoint exists.

categories.title: Branding & design

questions.question: Is there an existing brand (name, logo, colors) to follow, or should the design gallery propose fresh directions? Any apps whose look you love or hate?
questions.why: Feeds the design gallery so the mockups start close to your taste.

verify: Chosen fonts, colors and icon set from the design gallery are applied consistently.

categories.title: Testing
verify: Unit tests exist for core business logic.
At least one end-to-end test covers the main user flow.
Type checking passes with no errors.
